lessons: The premise holds. Every hub file, test_kill_signal_journal.py included, keeps `pytestmark = pytest.mark.disk_io_skip`. Its tests do not run. Scope out says skipped files may still break semantically and their batch ticket fixes that. Compatibility covers only tests that run today.

Write Rig in tests/misc_helpers.py on FakeFileSystem and FakeJournal, as Scope in says. Do not keep a separate real-I/O rig, and do not rewrite the hub tests. test_kill_signal_journal.py deletes its Rig and decision definitions and imports them back from tests.misc_helpers.

The run stopped before writing anything, so redo all the work. Create tests/misc_helpers.py with all 17 moved names. Repoint the importer lines in the fence. Have the 5 hubs import the names back. commit_lock returns asyncio.Lock(). test_git.py and the 8 real-I/O commit_lock importers stay

Add tests/unit/test_misc_helpers.py with one test per moved name, plus an import test. Assert that commit_lock(tmp_path/'state') is an asyncio.Lock and creates nothing, and that arrival writes only under tmp_path. Record the passed and skipped counts for the base commit and the candidate in run.md

Stop on a premise failure only when a test that runs today breaks, or when a shared fake lacks a behavior a helper needs. A helper change that only a skipped hub test notices is expected scope. Mention it under Surprises in run.md.
